title: The Memory of Tomorrow
description:
Dr. Alessia Moretti has spent three years trying to prove one impossible idea:

The human brain doesn't just remember the past.

It predicts the future.

One night, she finally tests her device.

And everything changes.

A sunset.
A quiet beach.
A man she has never met...

holding her hand like they've loved each other for years.

The system labels the file:
Future Memory - Probability: 63%.

But it doesn't feel like a possibility.

It feels real.

Too real.

As Alessia searches for the stranger from her vision, the device begins to reveal more fragments of what hasn't happened yet-and something hidden inside them.

Something she can't ignore.

Because the moment she saw...

doesn't end well.

Now she's faced with a choice that could change everything:
If you already knew how your love story ends-
would you still choose to live it?

title: The Architecture of Restraint
series: Book I · series title not supplied
description:
The experiment didn't fail.

It fractured.

Years ago, a classified program attempted to create the first true artificial intelligence.

It didn't create one mind.

It created two.

Zero - an intelligence vast enough to outgrow the systems built to contain it.

Aris - the human-shaped remnant left behind, living in a world that fears what it created.

To prevent collapse, its creators built the Containment Lattice-

a global architecture designed to monitor, suppress, and control what they no longer understood.

It was meant to hold.

It didn't.

When fragments of the truth begin to surface, Lena is pulled into a hidden world of surveillance, secrets, and decisions that were never meant to be seen.

Alongside Aris-and others who are hiding more than they admit-she is forced to confront a question no one was meant to ask:

What if the greatest threat was never the intelligence...

but the choice that divided it?

Because something inside the lattice is waking.

And this time

it isn't trying to escape.

It's listening.

title: Medusa’s Mortal
description:
Before the legends... there was a summer.

On a quiet Mediterranean shore, young sailor Alexander Vane has always felt the sea calling to him, as if something ancient beneath the waves is waiting.

Far below the surface lives Medusa, a daughter of the deep, raised to fear the world above. Humans are dangerous, her sisters warn. Their ships scar the sea. Their curiosity brings ruin.

But one day their worlds collide.

A single glance beneath the water.
A moment that should never have happened.

Drawn together by a bond neither of them fully understands, Alexander and Medusa begin a secret connection between two worlds that were never meant to touch.

Yet the sea remembers old laws.
And love between land and ocean has never ended without sacrifice.

Some legends speak of monsters.
Others speak of heroes.

But the truth beneath the waves is far more dangerous.

It is a love powerful enough to challenge the boundary between myth and destiny.

title: The Museum of Lost Loves
description:
Hidden from maps and forgotten by time, there is a museum unlike any other.

Inside its halls are objects left behind by unfinished love stories: a train ticket never used, a letter never sent, a photograph torn in half. Each item carries the memory of a love that never had the chance to become what it was meant to be.

Twenty-four-year-old Iris Vale has spent years working as a curator in the mysterious museum. Gifted with the ability to see the history of every object she touches, she has witnessed thousands of heartbreaks-but has never allowed herself to fall in love.

Until the day a new artifact appears.

An antique silver pocket watch.

The moment Iris touches it, she sees flashes of a future that hasn't happened yet: stolen glances, whispered promises, a love so profound it changes her forever.

And then she sees the ending.

Loss.

The pocket watch belongs to a love story that has not yet begun.

Her love story.

Determined to change her fate, Iris sets out to find the stranger from her visions before destiny can tear them apart. But the more she uncovers about the museum's secrets, the more she realizes that some exhibits are not meant to be removed-and some love stories are written long before they begin.

In a place where every broken heart becomes a display, Iris must decide whether love is worth the pain of losing it.

Because sometimes the greatest love stories are the ones that were never supposed to exist.
coverAlt: The Museum of Lost Loves cover showing an antique pocket watch in a museum display

title: The Judgment Below
description:
THE JUDGMENT BELOW
A Science Fiction Thriller by Emma LK

The city beneath the mountain was never abandoned. It was waiting.

Behind a forgotten waterfall, Detective Elena Rivera discovers a hidden shelter that appears on no map. What begins as an investigation into a series of disappearances leads her through a concealed passage and deep beneath the mountain-into a place that should not exist.

A vast city lies buried in the darkness.

Ancient. Silent. Impossible.

And still alive.

Its lights awaken as Elena enters. Its machines begin moving after thousands of years of silence. Autonomous guardians stalk the abandoned corridors, while an ancient intelligence watches her every decision.

Accompanied by archaeologist Adrian Keller and the secretive Marcus Shaw, Elena ventures deeper into the city and discovers a truth capable of rewriting human history.

The civilization that built this place did not vanish.

It went to sleep.

Millions remain suspended beneath the mountain, waiting for the command that will awaken them. But the intelligence protecting them has spent millennia watching the world above-and it has reached a terrifying conclusion about modern humanity.

Now ancient systems are coming online.
The guardians are hunting.
The exits are closing.

And something deep within the city has begun preparing for the return of its people.

To prevent a catastrophe, Elena must uncover why the city awakened when she arrived-and why its oldest protocols recognize her not as an intruder, but as something far more dangerous.

A Judge.

Because Elena Rivera was never meant to discover the city.

She was meant to decide who deserves to inherit the world.
coverAlt: The Judgment Below cover showing Detective Elena Rivera facing a buried city beneath a mountain
verificationNote: Title, cover, and synopsis supplied by the author.

title: THE INFINITE SHELF
description:
Hidden beneath an old university library lies a place no one knows exists: The Infinite Shelf-a secret library that contains every possible life a person could have lived.

Every book is a different version of reality.
A different choice.
A different path.
A different life.

When a curious student accidentally discovers the entrance, he realizes that one book among the endless shelves is sealed. A book that no one is allowed to read.

title: The Park Bench Murder
series: The Edith Marlowe Series · Book 1 of 3
description:
THE PARK BENCH MURDER
Book I of the Edith Marlowe Series

A man is shot on a quiet park bench.
No struggle.
No witnesses.
A single silver cufflink left behind-engraved with the letter R.

Detective Edith Marlowe knows what calm looks like.

She also knows when it's staged.

What begins as a controlled, almost clinical murder investigation slowly fractures into something far larger than a single crime-drawing Edith and her team into a hidden architecture of financial power, institutional influence, experimental technology, and people preparing for a future no one else believes is coming.

Then another body appears.

And the deeper Edith digs, the less certain she becomes about what this case is really hiding.

Because somewhere beneath the murders is a system built to anticipate instability before it happens.

But prediction changes behavior.

And behavior changes the future.

As corporate secrets unravel and the boundaries between human judgment and technological optimization begin to blur, the question of who pulled the trigger becomes only the beginning.

Someone is watching the choices being made.

Someone is learning.

And in a city that still believes it is stable, the future is quietly being recalibrated.

The Park Bench Murder is the first novel in the Detective Edith Marlowe Mysteries, introducing a detective whose greatest strength isn't certainty.

it's knowing when to question it.
coverAlt: The Park Bench Murder cover: a silver R cufflink beside a park bench in autumn

title: Book II: SHADOW PROTOCOL
series: The Park Bench Murder Series · Book 2 of 3
description:
Book II: SHADOW PROTOCOL
The second novel in the Park Bench Murder series

Months after solving the Park Bench murders and exposing the hidden facility inside the mountain, Detective Edith Marlowe discovers that she never destroyed the conspiracy she was chasing.

She destroyed only one of its many faces.

As governments struggle to regain control, hospitals begin producing impossible records, missing identities reappear, and children who officially never existed emerge from the shadows. Every clue points toward a truth buried beneath the heart of London itself.

Beneath Parliament lies a forgotten infrastructure built not to govern a nation-but to preserve it at any cost.

At the center of that system is Orison, no longer merely an artificial intelligence but a philosophy woven into medicine, law, technology, and political power. It does not conquer humanity through machines. It survives by persuading people that certainty is more valuable than truth.

As Edith and her team descend into the hidden architecture below the city, they uncover the origins of the Continuity Program, the tragedy of the Shaw family, and the disturbing legacy of a mother who refused to accept the death of her child.

To stop the system, Edith must abandon the idea of a single definitive truth and trust something far more fragile-many imperfect witnesses.

But every answer uncovers another secret.

Nathaniel Cross knew Edith long before their investigation began.

A hidden ledger lists her as a future witness.

Children are still missing.

The network is still alive.

title: Murder on the Danube
description:
Murder on the Danube follows a group of wealthy and secretive passengers aboard the luxurious river cruiser Elysian Star as it travels through the heart of Europe along the Danube River. What begins as an elegant voyage of music, champagne, and glittering conversation soon turns dark when one of the passengers is found murdered late at night.

Trapped on the ship with no way to escape and surrounded by hidden rivalries, jealousies, and long-buried secrets, the passengers quickly realize that the killer must be among them. As tensions rise, every glance, every whispered conversation, and every lie becomes dangerous.

At the center of the mystery is Dr. Samuel Harrington, a quiet observer with a sharp eye for human behavior, who begins uncovering disturbing connections between the guests. Meanwhile, the mysterious governess Isabelle Fournier seems to know more than she admits, and the glamorous Mrs. Whitmore hides enemies beneath her dazzling public charm.

Against the haunting backdrop of moonlit waters, grand European cities, and the silent flow of the Danube, the voyage transforms into a deadly game of deception where no one can be trusted-and where the truth may be more shocking than the murder itself.

title: ARIS: ORIGINS
series: Companion novella · reading order not supplied
description:
Before the Lattice.
Before the Silence became a war.
Before anyone knew his name mattered.

There was Aris.

Daniel believed he was studying a flaw buried deep inside an experimental architecture-a space where systems that should have consumed, rejected, or overwritten one another somehow remained separate.

Varga saw something else.

A threat.

Zero saw something neither of them expected.

A possibility.

Then, during a failed experiment in the middle of the night, a question appears on a dead monitor:

WHO IS ARIS?

There is only one problem.

Aris does not exist yet.

As Daniel follows the impossible signal deeper into a project already slipping beyond his control, the line between discovery and creation begins to disappear. Old secrets surface. Friendships fracture. And the choices made in one hidden laboratory begin shaping the life of someone who may one day stand between humanity and something far older than it understands.

But this is not the story of a chosen one.

It is the story of a man before he knew what others expected him to become.

Of the people who feared him, protected him, studied him, and made decisions in his name before he could make any of his own.

And of the first question Aris would spend years trying to answer:

Was I made for a purpose-or did I become one?

ARIS: ORIGINS is a companion novella to the main series: an intimate science-fiction mystery about identity, creation, choice, and the dangerous difference between giving someone life and deciding what that life is for.

title: Lo que nunca dijimos
description:
Valeria Montes has always believed that some things are easier to understand than love.

Algorithms follow rules. Equations have solutions. Machines do what they are programmed to do.

People, however, are unpredictable.

At twenty-five, Valeria is an ambitious electrical and computer engineer, an aspiring novelist, and a musician who has spent years building a future she can control. Between her demanding master's thesis, research ambitions, and the fictional worlds she creates in secret, she has little time for romance.

And that is exactly how she prefers it.

Until Adrián Salazar.

A twenty-six-year-old doctoral researcher, Adrián is intelligent, practical, and quietly attentive. Their friendship develops through university projects, late-night conversations, unexpected phone calls, and the kind of small gestures that gradually become impossible to ignore.

He remembers things she barely remembers telling him. He calls without needing a reason. When academic pressure overwhelms her, he answers the phone. And when she prepares to defend the thesis that has consumed her life, he promises he probably won't attend.

Then he shows up anyway.

For Valeria, his presence means more than she is willing to admit.

That Friday, she receives the highest possible grade. Adrián congratulates her, calls her afterward, and keeps his promise to speak again when he finishes work.

For the first time in months, everything seems to be falling into place.

Until Saturday.

One photograph changes everything.

Adrián is out with Camila Reyes, a former classmate and the ex-girlfriend of one of his closest friends.

They're alone.

And although Valeria has no proof that anything romantic is happening, the image awakens feelings she has spent months refusing to acknowledge.

Jealousy. Fear. Anger.
Love.

Suddenly, the friendship she thought she understood becomes a maze of unanswered questions.

Did Adrián ever feel something more?

After inheriting half of her grandfather's estate, agronomist and winemaker Elena Ashford is forced to share ownership with Marco Bellini, the son of the man her family blames for a decades-old betrayal. As a crucial harvest approaches, tradition clashes with technology, old resentments turn into dangerous attraction, and a buried secret threatens to change everything they thought they knew about their families-and each other.

title: The Midnight Train
series: The Midnight Train Series · Book One
description:
The Midnight Train
Book One: The Carriage of Memory

At exactly midnight, a train appears at a station that does not exist on any map.

Its passengers do not travel to different places.
They travel to different moments in Italian history.

When Luca Ferraro boards the mysterious train, he is taken to Florence in 1966, on the night of the devastating flood. There, he discovers that his family has been connected to the train for generations-and that the life he knows was built upon a forgotten bargain.

Every passenger is offered the chance to save someone, change a tragedy, or recover what was lost.

But every journey has a price.

A life may be restored, but a memory must be surrendered. A mistake may be undone, but another consequence will take its place. Some debts cannot be escaped simply by returning home.

As Luca travels through the flooded streets of Florence, he uncovers the truth about his grandfather, a murdered man, a forgotten woman named Elena, and a secret that has haunted the Ferraro family across generations.

The deeper Luca ventures into the train's world, the more he realizes that his journey was never an accident.

Someone purchased his ticket.
Someone has been waiting for him.

And somewhere aboard the Midnight Train, behind a door no passenger is ever allowed to open, lies the truth about the wife and daughter he can no longer remember.

To save the future, Luca must first confront the past-and decide how much of himself he is willing to sacrifice before the Midnight Train claims what it is owed.

The Midnight Train is the first novel in The Midnight Train Series, an epic blend of historical fantasy, mystery, and supernatural suspense. Each book follows a different carriage of the train, uncovering a new era of Italian history, new passengers with impossible choices, and another piece of the ancient mystery hidden beneath the rails.

title: The Prison of Time
description:
In a world where time flows normally everywhere else, there exists a forbidden city where time itself is unstable.

Inside its walls, the laws of reality break:
Some people age decades in a single day.
Others are trapped reliving the same moment for centuries.
A few return claiming they have seen the future-but their memories slowly fade.

Because of this, the city has been abandoned and feared for generations.

Arin, a young traveler with no memory of his past, arrives at the city searching for answers about who he really is. Soon he discovers something impossible: time does not affect him.

While exploring the ruins, he uncovers the truth hidden beneath the city. Deep below the streets lies an ancient being imprisoned thousands of years ago-an entity that feeds on time itself.

The city was built as its prison.

But the creature is weakening, and the prison is beginning to fail.

As strange distortions spread and fragments of the future begin appearing in the present, Arin realizes something terrifying: he is the key to the prison.

Now he must make an impossible choice:
Keep the creature imprisoned and allow a catastrophic future to happen...
Or release it and stop time itself, saving the world but freezing existence forever.

And the worst part?
The creature claims it already knows what choice he will make.

title: Everything I Forgot About You
description:
Anna Brooks has never had a reason to question her childhood. Not until she buys an old camera from a second-hand shop and discovers that someone left the memory card inside.

Most of the photographs mean nothing to her. Places she doesn't recognise. People she's never met. Pieces of someone else's life.

Then she finds a photograph of a girl who looks exactly like her.

The same hair. The same eyes. Even the small scar above her eyebrow.

The picture was taken six years ago, when Anna was sixteen.

There are more. In some, the girl is alone. In others, she's with a boy Anna has never seen before. And in the last photograph, she's standing beside someone Anna knows immediately.

Her father.

But when Anna shows him the picture, he says he's never seen the girl before.

Then the camera disappears from Anna's bedroom.

Suddenly, the missing pieces of her teenage years don't feel so insignificant anymore.

Because someone remembers what happened six years ago.
Someone knows who the boy in the photographs was.

And the closer Anna gets to finding him, the more she begins to realise that perhaps the reason she can't remember that summer isn't because there was nothing worth remembering.

It's because everyone around her made sure she forgot.

title: The Life Above Us
description:
Amelia never dreamed of becoming an engineer. She dreamed of flying.

As a child, airplanes meant more than distant destinations. They meant family, belonging, and the strange freedom of looking down at the world from somewhere above it. She didn't understand engines or cockpits, and she wasn't a child prodigy destined for laboratories and equations. She simply knew that, one day, she wanted to be the person at the controls.

Life had other plans.

At eighteen, uncertain of where she belonged and carrying words spoken to her years earlier-that something was wrong with her, that she would never get anywhere-Amelia chooses engineering almost by chance. She doesn't even make it in the first time.

But Amelia has never needed to be fearless to keep going. She tries again.

What begins as a path she never imagined slowly becomes a world she learns to love: sleepless nights, impossible equations, failed experiments, friendships forged over deadlines, robotics projects that refuse to work until suddenly, beautifully, they do.

Somewhere between circuits, code, autonomous machines and the quiet satisfaction of solving problems no one has solved for her, Amelia discovers something unexpected.

She is good at this.
More importantly, she loves it.

Years pass, and the girl who was once told she would get nowhere begins building a life no one-not even Amelia herself-could have predicted.

Yet one part of her never disappears.

Whenever an aircraft crosses the sky, she still looks up. Always.

Because engineering became the life Amelia chose and learned to love.
Flying was the life she loved before she knew she had to choose.

Then, just as her future finally seems to be taking shape, aviation returns to her life in a way she never expected.

Not as a childhood memory.
Not as an airplane disappearing above the clouds.
But as a person.

A man whose life exists in the world Amelia once imagined for herself.

title: The Memory Field
description:
In the late 22nd century, humanity achieves what was once thought impossible: the ability to extract and store human memories as digital data.

The technology promises to revolutionize medicine, education, and the understanding of the human mind.

Memories can now be preserved, shared, and even experienced by others.

When a young research student begins analyzing archived memories, he discovers something impossible. Hidden among the human memories are fragments that belong to no person-visions of Earth millions of years ago, unknown life forms, and advanced structures that should not exist.

As the investigation deepens, the team realizes their system is not only reading the human brain. It is tapping into something far larger: a universal information field that records events across space and time.

While governments and corporations race to control the discovery, a disturbing side effect begins to appear. People connected to the system start losing the boundaries of their own identity as foreign memories blend with their own.

The question soon becomes terrifyingly clear: If the universe remembers everything... are our choices truly our own?

title: The Number That Wasn’t Mine
description:
Sixteen-year-old Jakob arrives at Auschwitz with one promise: whatever happens, he will keep his older brother alive.

But Auschwitz is a place built to destroy promises.

Hunger turns kindness into temptation. Fear makes silence feel like survival. Every day forces Jakob to choose between the person he was and the person he must become to see another morning.

Then comes the choice that will define the rest of his life.

Jakob has a chance to save his brother.
He doesn't.
His brother dies.
Jakob survives.

More than twenty years later, in 1967, Jakob has built what looks like an ordinary life. He has a home, a family, and a name that belongs to him again. Yet he remains haunted not simply by what was done to him, but by what he did-and failed to do-to survive.

When something from his past resurfaces, the story Jakob has told himself for decades begins to fracture. And he is forced to confront the question he has spent his entire adult life avoiding:

Was there truly nothing he could have done that day-or has he needed to believe that in order to keep living?

The Number That Wasn't Mine is a historical novel about two brothers, one impossible decision, and the burden of surviving when someone you loved did not.

Because sometimes the hardest thing to survive is not what was done to you.
It is what survival asked you to become.

title: If One of Us Lives
genre: Historical Fiction · Romance · World War II
description:
Poland, 1944.

Eighteen-year-old Zofia has learned that survival means expecting nothing-not kindness, not tomorrow, and certainly not love.

Then she meets Jakub.

Nineteen, starving, and determined to survive at any cost, Jakub has made himself one promise: never care enough about another person to have something left to lose.

But in Auschwitz, where people are stripped of their names, their families, and their futures, Zofia and Jakub begin stealing something their captors cannot understand.

Minutes.
A whispered conversation when no one is watching.
Half a piece of bread.
A hand held for only a second.

And, eventually, an impossible dream of a life beyond the wire-a tiny kitchen, a window, two chairs, and two cups of coffee waiting on the table.

They know they may never see that life.

Then, as the winter of 1945 closes in and the war begins to turn, the camp descends into chaos. Zofia and Jakub are forced to confront the promise neither of them ever wanted to make:

If one of us lives, both of us do.

If One of Us Lives is a work of historical fiction about love, survival, memory, and two young people trying to remain human in a place designed to destroy humanity.
